gaps.description: Scribe has no default values or keyword-only parameters. hi and key become maybe parameters, and every caller must pass lo, hi and key explicitly (0, nothing, nothing for the common case).

gaps.construct: key is a function passed as an argument and called as key(a[mid])
gaps.description: The doc has no type for an operation value and never shows a bound name being called. 'Operation from T to K' and the call 'key_function (item mid of a)' are invented.

gaps.construct: a may hold any type that supports __lt__; x is compared with elements or with key results
gaps.description: Example 9 shows a type parameter T but no way to constrain it to ordered types, or to declare it on an operation. 'given T is an Ordered type' is invented.

gaps.construct: x has the element type when key is None and the key's result type otherwise
gaps.description: A parameter's type cannot depend on whether another optional argument was supplied; the translation types x as K and relies on K being T when key is nothing, which nothing in the doc enforces.

gaps.construct: if hi is None: hi = len(a)
gaps.description: There is no 'value or default' expression for a maybe. choose is a statement, so a var is created and then set in both branches.

gaps.construct: parameters lo and hi are rebound as loop variables
gaps.description: Parameters are read-only by default, so new vars low and high are introduced. Clear but adds two lines.
The doc uses '/' on Int in example 10 as if it were integer division, but never says whether '/' on Int truncates, floors, or produces a fraction.

gaps.construct: Python ints are unbounded; lo + hi never overflows
gaps.description: Scribe has checked arithmetic, but the doc does not say whether a checked-overflow failure must be listed in 'fails with', or how big Int is.

gaps.construct: raise ValueError('lo must be non-negative'); a[mid] raises IndexError if hi > len(a)
gaps.description: The doc shows failures as bare names with no message, and does not say what 'item i of items' does when i is out of range (a failure? a precondition?).

gaps.construct: docstring: all e in a[:i] have e <= x, all e in a[i:] have e > x; 'assuming a is sorted'
gaps.description: The named predicate 'is sorted' is defined only for List of Int and cannot be parameterised by a key; the postcondition only matches the docstring for the full-range, no-key case.

invented_syntax: given T is an Ordered type
given key is a maybe Operation from T to K
key_function (item mid of a)  (calling an operation held in a variable)
fail with ValueError because "..."  (because on a fail line)
notes: bisect_right is the motivating case for defaults plus higher-order parameters: its common call is bisect_right(a, x), but in Scribe it becomes a six-argument call. The doc's own binary search (example 10) has the same shape, so the body itself translated cleanly; all the friction is in the header. The duplicated loop for the key case is kept to match the original, which duplicates it for speed.
